skill.name: datadog-automation
skill.description: Use Rube MCP to automate Datadog metrics, logs, monitors, dashboards, events, downtimes, hosts, and traces.
skill.summary: Guides Datadog observability workflows through Rube MCP tool sequences.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static external command and blocker alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and Datadog identifiers in documentation. The confirmed static issue is the Rube MCP URL, which is an expected external network dependency. A semantic risk remains because the skill enables privileged Datadog changes such as muting monitors, deleting dashboards, and creating downtimes.

remediation.suggestion: Document the Rube MCP trust boundary and tell users to review permissions before connecting Datadog.
Require explicit confirmation before update, mute, downtime, or delete actions. Show affected resources, scope, and expiration.
Default to scoped tags, short time ranges, and downtime end times. Warn before broad scopes or missing end times.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Datadog connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `datadog`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
- Query syntax follows Datadog's metric query format: `aggregation:metric_name{tag_filters}`
- `from` and `to` are Unix epoch timestamps in seconds, not milliseconds
2. `DATADOG_SEARCH_LOGS` - Search logs with query and filters [Required]
- `query`: Log search query using Datadog log query syntax
- `limit`: Number of log entries to return
- Log queries use Datadog's log search syntax: `service:web status:error`
- `type`: Monitor type ('metric alert', 'service check', 'log alert', 'query alert', etc.)
- `query`: Monitor query defining the alert condition
- Monitor `type` must match the query type; mismatches cause creation failures
- Thresholds vary by monitor type; metric monitors need `critical` at minimum
- `layout_type` cannot be changed after creation; must recreate the dashboard
- `end`: End time (Unix epoch; omit for indefinite)
- `monitor_id`: Specific monitor to downtime (optional, omit for scope-based)
- Event `text` supports Datadog's markdown format including @mentions
- Omitting `end` creates an indefinite downtime; always set an end time for maintenance
- Downtime `monitor_id` narrows to a single monitor; scope applies to all matching monitors
- `trace_id`: Distributed trace ID for trace lookup
- Use `page` and `page_size` or offset-based pagination depending on endpoint
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k

content.user_title: Automate Datadog Operations with Rube MCP
content.value_statement: Datadog workflows often require switching between metrics, logs, monitors, dashboards, and maintenance pages. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through Rube MCP tool sequences.
actual_capabilities: Search current Rube Datadog tool schemas before running workflows.
Query Datadog metrics and list available metric names.
Search Datadog logs and list log indexes.
List, inspect, create, update, mute, and unmute monitors.
List, inspect, update, and delete dashboards.
Create events, schedule downtimes, list hosts, and fetch traces.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP and an active Datadog connection.
Does not include Datadog credentials or direct API client code.
Tool schemas can change, so tools must be searched first.
Destructive actions depend on Datadog permissions and operator approval.

use_cases.title: Investigate Service Health
use_cases.description: Query metrics, logs, and monitors for a service during an incident.

use_cases.title: Prepare Maintenance Windows
use_cases.description: Create scoped downtimes and events for planned infrastructure work.

use_cases.title: Maintain Observability Assets
use_cases.description: Review monitors and dashboards before updating operational coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Check Service Health
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Datadog automation skill for service <service> in <environment>. Search Rube tools first. Query metrics, logs, and monitors for the last <duration>. Summarize findings before changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Monitor
prompt_templates.prompt: Search current Datadog tool schemas. Draft a monitor for <signal> on <service>. Include query, thresholds, message, tags, and notification targets. Ask for approval before creation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Downtime
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Datadog downtime tools. Prepare a downtime for scope <scope> from <start> to <end>. Include affected monitors, message, and rollback checks. Request confirmation before scheduling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Incident Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Rube Datadog tools, then review metrics, logs, monitors, dashboards, events, hosts, and traces for <system>. Identify coverage gaps. Propose changes without executing them.

output_examples.input: Investigate elevated latency for checkout in production for the last hour.
output: Tool schemas checked and Datadog connection verified.
Metrics showed latency rising after deployment start.
Logs showed timeout errors concentrated on checkout workers.
Recommended next step: review the recent deployment and inspect the related monitor.

output_examples.input: Prepare a downtime for database maintenance tonight.
output: Prepared a scoped downtime plan with a defined start and end time.
Included the target scope, maintenance message, and affected monitor review.
Waiting for explicit approval before scheduling the downtime.

output_examples.input: Review dashboard cleanup options for obsolete staging services.
output: Listed candidate dashboards and checked their service tags.
Flagged dashboards with recent activity for retention.
Marked delete actions as pending approval because deletion is permanent.

best_practices: Search current Rube tool schemas before each Datadog workflow.
Review every monitor, downtime, and dashboard change before execution.
Use narrow tags, short time windows, and downtime end times.
anti_patterns: Running delete, mute, or downtime actions without explicit approval.
Assuming tool schemas from memory instead of searching Rube tools.
Using broad scopes or long time ranges when a narrow query works.

faq.question: Does this skill require Datadog API keys?
faq.answer: No API keys are stored in the skill. It requires an active Datadog connection through Rube MCP.

faq.question: Can Claude use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it create or change monitors?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide monitor creation, updates, muting, and unmuting when Datadog permissions allow it.

faq.question: Can it delete dashboards?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes dashboard deletion guidance, so users should require explicit approval.

faq.question: Why does it search tools first?
faq.answer: Rube MCP tool schemas can change. Searching first helps Codex or Claude Code use current parameters.

faq.question: What should I verify before running actions?
faq.answer: Verify the Datadog connection, target scope, time range, affected resources, and approval for mutable changes.
